canonical_name: lru-cache -- a C++ LRU cache (Peter Goldsborough)
lineage: LRU (least-recently-used) eviction: when a bounded cache is full, discard the entry unused for longest; a hash-map + intrusive list, the standard caching mechanism across CPUs, OSes and databases
version: github.com/goldsborough/lru-cache master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
entry_points: LRU::Cache<K,V> insert/find/contains with a capacity bound

example.command: Techne driver: fill past capacity, verify the least-recently-used key is the one evicted; then a THRASH pattern (working set > capacity) showing near-zero hit rate
example.output: hit/miss counts; the evicted key on overflow

human_capability_summary.built_to: keep the most useful bounded subset of data in fast memory by evicting the least-recently-used entry when capacity is exceeded
human_capability_summary.pressure: memory/cache far smaller than the data; every miss costs a slow fetch, so the eviction choice determines performance
human_capability_summary.success_means: a high hit rate on workloads with temporal locality, within a fixed capacity

human_environmental_pressure: bounded memory, a working set larger than capacity, temporal-locality (or its absence)
human_failure_condition: cache thrashing: when the working set exceeds capacity and locality is poor, the hit rate collapses toward zero and the cache is pure overhead
behavioral_entry_point: access a working set LARGER than the capacity (the harness does this) to induce thrashing -- a pathological-behavior receipt

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run lru-cache-goldsborough
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: keep the most useful bounded subset of data in fast memory by evicting the least-recently-used entry when capacity is exceeded
